strategy.observation: Linear’s product work is already deeply embedded in Notion: its integration supports pasting Linear links as live previews, /linear commands, and an AI connector that lets Notion users search Linear projects, issues, and comments, with previews that update as issue properties change.
strategy.offer_link: Because Linear already uses Notion as a working layer for product information, a service that recruits and schedules customer interview participants could fit as an operational add-on for the product team—freeing them to turn that centralized workflow into a steadier stream of customer feedback without handling the logistics themselves.
hypotheses: The Head of Product at Linear may be responsible for customer discovery or for ensuring product teams get regular user feedback.
Linear may use Notion as a coordination hub beyond issue tracking, including research notes or interview planning.
The team may care about reducing the operational burden of sourcing and scheduling interview participants.
strategy.angle: Notion already carries a lot of Linear’s product context; if your team is also using it to coordinate customer interviews, we could handle recruiting and scheduling the participants.
strategy.fit_reason: The facts show a strong Notion/Linear workflow, but they do not show any current customer-research process or interview program. Recruiting and scheduling interview participants could help a product team, but the link to this specific company and recipient is indirect, so the fit is plausible but not strong.

draft.subject: Linear interviews in Notion
draft.body:
Linear’s Notion integration supports live previews for issues, projects, and views, and those previews update when properties change. It also supports the /linear command in Notion, and the AI Connector lets Notion users search Linear projects, issues, and comments.

If Notion is also where your team plans customer interviews, we could handle recruiting and scheduling the participants. That would keep the logistics out of the product team’s hands.

Worth a quick look?
